title: What If a Mountain Fell on a Sleeping Town? In 1903 It Took 100 Seconds

scenes.text: What if a mountain fell on a sleeping town? In 1903, one did in about 100 seconds.
At 4:10 a.m. on April 29th, the face of Turtle Mountain broke loose above Frank, Alberta.
Roughly a hundred million tons of limestone crossed the valley at about 70 miles an hour.
It buried three square kilometers. Of about 100 people in its path, at least 70 died.
Seventeen miners were sealed inside the mountain. Thirteen hours later, they dug themselves out.
The Blackfoot and Kutenai already called it the mountain that moves. It's still monitored today, because scientists expect it to fall again.

description:
What if a mountain fell on a sleeping town? At 4:10 a.m. on 29 April 1903 the east face of Turtle Mountain collapsed onto the coal town of Frank, Alberta, in about 100 seconds.
The Frank Slide Interpretive Centre puts the rock at about 110 million tonnes (the Canadian Encyclopedia says 82 million), moving at up to 120 km/h and covering three square kilometers. Of roughly 100 people in its path, between 70 and more than 90 died; 17 miners trapped inside dug their own way out after 13 hours. The mountain's unstable structure was the main cause, with mining and a freeze after a wet winter contributing, and it is monitored in real time today.
